title: Cohort fractionation simulator & ops playbook (personal)
content:
Quick intent
- Small personal scratchpad to capture a lightweight simulator for fractional/cohort rollouts, plus an ops checklist and failure-mode responses. Not an org canonical doc — meant for on-call and quick-run planning before formalizing into a Confluence page.

Goals for this approach
- Reduce blast radius for model or runtime changes by splitting traffic into small independent cohorts that are easy to shift back.
- Make thresholds and actions explicit so an on-call engineer can act without hunting context.
- Provide a fast way to rehearse rollouts locally with a tiny simulator that mirrors our rate-limited, latency-sensitive routing.

High-level rollout model
- Start with 0.5% of user sessions => expand in multiples (0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10) depending on stability.
- Cohorts are assigned deterministically via user_id hash + cohort salt; cohorts are attached to the routing layer.
- For each cohort fraction we maintain: expected qps, expected p90 latency, error-rate tolerance, fresh-cache hit rate.

Signals we watch (primary -> action)
- request_error_rate (5m window): >1.0% for 5m -> pause expansion, revert new model to previous variant for that cohort.
- model_confidence_regressions (rolling eval): Delta >3% vs baseline -> hold and trigger eval job.
- p95 latency: +30% vs baseline for 3m -> reduce cohort fraction by 50% or divert to fallback model.
- downstream_throttle_signals (GPUs/OOMs): any non-zero repeated 3 times -> immediate hold and notify infra.
- semantic_quality_alerts (ops or CS reported): manual hold and tag cohort for human review.

Quick threshold matrix (defaults)
- tiny cohort (0.5%): error 1.0%, p95 +50% -> immediate revert
- small cohort (1-2%): error 0.8%, p95 +40% -> hold and investigate
- medium cohort (5%): error 0.5%, p95 +30% -> hold and maybe shift 2x smaller cohorts back to baseline
- ramp stop always if >=2 signals fire within a 10-minute window.

Simulator (pseudo-runbook)
- purpose: locally approximate effect of cohort changes on traffic and heavy-tail latencies. Good for rehearsing commands and expected alerts.
- inputs: baseline_qps, cohort_fraction, baseline_p95, baseline_error_rate, burst_factor
- simple step logic:
  1) cohort_qps = baseline_qps * cohort_fraction
  2) expected_error = baseline_error + (0.0001 * burst_factor * cohort_qps / 100)
  3) expected_p95 = baseline_p95 * (1 + 0.1 * burst_factor)
  4) if expected_error > threshold_error OR expected_p95 > threshold_p95: mark cohort as "unhealthy"
- practice runs: run with baseline_qps=5000, cohort_fraction=0.01 (1%), burst_factor [0,1,3] to see how sensitive thresholds are.

Ops checklist (pre-rollout)
- [ ] Confirm canary cohort routing is active in staging and mirrors prod hashing (test with checksum tool).
- [ ] Smoke tests: canonical prompt set (20 prompts) run against service with new model and baseline; capture embeddings/diff.
- [ ] Ensure cache-warmers are scheduled for cohorts that rely on prefix caching (run warmup job with sample prefixes).
- [ ] Confirm alerts exist and notify #releases + oncall.
- [ ] Ensure rollback commands exist and one person is assigned as owner for first 30 minutes of the rollout.

Rollout commands (quick)
- enable cohort fraction 1%: infractl roll cohort set --cohort-id fractional-A --fraction 0.01 --model new-model:v42
- reduce fraction by half: infractl roll cohort set --cohort-id fractional-A --fraction 0.005
- detach cohort -> baseline: infractl roll cohort set --cohort-id fractional-A --model baseline-model:stable
- force revert all cohorts to baseline: infractl roll cohort revert --tag stable --reason "auto-revert"
- check cohort assignment: infractl roll cohort status --cohort-id fractional-A

Example timeline (30-min micro ramp template)
- T+00:00: start 0.5% cohort (owner: Lena O.). Smoke tests run, alerts observed.
- T+00:10: if no signals -> bump to 1.0%. Run quick eval.
- T+00:20: if no signals and quality flags clear -> bump to 2.0% else hold and investigate.
- T+00:30: either continue to scheduled ramp or begin staged backfill depending on telemetry.

Failure-mode quick playbook
- sudden error spike without latency increase: check downstream dependency flaps (KV, auth). If dependency degraded, temporarily divert cohort to read-only fallback model.
- latency degradation without error increase: check GPU utilization and KV cache hit rates. If cache warmup low -> run cache warmer then hold expansion.
- semantic regression flagged by CS: pause ramp, snapshot failing prompts and escalate to model owner + ML research for triage.
- progressive slow bleed of small errors over weeks: open a regression ticket, schedule re-eval against 1k longitudinal prompts, consider rolling back model variant.

Notes on pinning strategy
- prefer model-pin per-route (route-level model attribute) instead of global env pin. Easier to roll back per feature.
- pin metadata should include commit SHA, qkv quantization profile, and a human-readable build tag.
- always version two previous stable variants in the routing config so we can fall back without redeploy.

Observability checklist (telemetry to have pre-roll)
- cohort traffic % metric broken out by route/model
- request_error_rate (5m and 30m) per cohort
- p50/p95/p99 per cohort and per model variant
- cache_hit_rate by prefix length per cohort
- GPU saturation and host-level OOM logs correlated to cohort events
- anomaly detection alerts wired for sudden shifts in embedding norms (drift detector).

Handy debug commands + queries
- quickly list active cohorts: infractl roll cohort list --env prod
- time series (last 15m) error rate for cohort: metectl query "errors{cohort=\"fractional-A\"}" --range 15m
- compare model outputs for sample prompts (local python): python tools/compare_outputs.py --model a:v41 --model b:stable --prompts sample_prompts.json

Open questions / TODOs
- Find a clean way to automatically annotate rollout signals with the cohort hash so we can query traces by cohort id (is the trace header already propagated?).
- Decide whether per-cohort cache warmers should run on every expansion step or only on first creation. Cost vs latency tradeoff.
- Add a small synthetic-traffic job that mimics tail latency bursts to staging so we can rehearse p95 regressions.

Last quick run notes from a practice session (2024-11-22)
- ran a 1% cohort with a debug model that had an op-level change; saw p95 jump 35% only under burst_factor=3. The simulator predicted the jump correctly.
- alerting threshold for small cohorts felt noisy; we should try smoothing error rate with a 3-minute rolling average before firing auto-holds.
- cache warmer reduced tail latency for templated prompts significantly — recommend enabling warmers for any cohort >1%.

If I get time
- wrap the simulator into a tiny CLI that can produce a quick runbook PDF (inputs + expected actions).
- formalize the matrix and push to Confluence with a short TL;DR for oncall.

End of scratchpad.

(Keep this informal — will convert to a team doc once we validate simulator behavior in staging.)
